--- marp: true title: "Anthropic PBC: the public record in charts" paginate: true size: 16:9 style: | section { background: #fcfcfb; color: #0b0b0b; font-family: "DejaVu Sans", system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 26px; padding: 48px 64px; } h1 { font-size: 40px; margin-bottom: 8px; } h2 { font-size: 30px; margin: 0 0 12px; } p, li { line-height: 1.35; } section.chart { padding: 32px 48px; } section.chart img { display: block; margin: 0 auto; max-height: 520px; } .src { font-size: 15px; color: #52514e; position: absolute; bottom: 28px; left: 48px; right: 120px; } .tag { font-size: 16px; color: #52514e; } --- # Anthropic PBC ## The public record in charts Built from commit `23a4bb63cc0f` with risk codebook **v0.2-draft** (DRAFT: wording awaits review). Every number on these slides is read from a committed table at build time. Model labels come from two NLI witnesses; a label counts only when both score it ≥ 0.5. Labels are proposals, not hand-verified findings: there is no gold set yet. --- ## The argument (edition v0 of the paper) **Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.** - §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest - The public the charter names cannot enforce it. Edition v0 of the paper (`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` at `1afb042`) rests on Anthropic's own filings. This deck looks outward at public data. --- ![w:900](deck/ai-risk-by-year.svg)
AI framed as a risk: 12.2% of 2026 S&P 500 calls (to 2026-11-04), against at most 0.6% in any year before 2023.
--- ![h:520](deck/risk-ranking-ttm.svg)
137 firms raised AI as a risk in the 12 months to 2026-11-04. Most named: Cybersecurity (40), Safety / ethics / misuse (31), Overspending / capex return (26).
--- ![h:520](deck/intent-ttm.svg)
Analysts ask how AI sells (21.2% of AI questions) far more than how its risk is controlled (0.8%). Question-intent codebook v0.1.
--- ![h:540](deck/dialogue-space.svg)
Safety and ethics: 10% of executives' AI-risk passages, 39% on Hacker News about Anthropic, 61% on Wikipedia. Cyber dominates HN's AI-security set (85%).
--- ![w:950](deck/cve-ai-credit.svg)
CVE credits name Claude on 370 CVEs and any AI system on 924 (2020-01 to 2026-10). That cannot confirm or refute "33,000+": not every flaw becomes a CVE, and credits need not name the tool.
--- ## What this deck does not show - **No effect of Anthropic on any outcome.** Attention and counts only. - **No gold set yet.** Witness precision is unmeasured. - **Survivorship.** The earnings-call universe is today's S&P 500. - **No news-attention chart.** GDELT's daily series omits days, so it is not used. - **Draft codebook.** Wording of v0.2-draft awaits human review. Sources, licences and rebuild commands: `DATASETS.md`. Build stamp: `deck/STAMP.json`.

# Hacker News: Anthropic and AI-security comments (IDs only)

Two focused sets of Hacker News comments, January 2021 to August 2026: those
that mention Anthropic or Claude, and those about AI security incidents (CVEs,
breaches, prompt injection, jailbreaks, leaked weights or keys). Method:
[`docs/hacker-news-corpus.md`](../../docs/hacker-news-corpus.md).

**No comment text and no usernames are stored here.** HN commenters are mostly
private individuals, so this folder holds item ids, character offsets into a
deterministic normalisation of each comment, and BLAKE3 hashes. The text is
rebuilt locally from the pinned source into the gitignored `.hncorpus/`, and
`verify` checks every hash. Any comment can be read at
`https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<item_id>`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: 68 monthly parquet files of `open-index/hacker-news` at dataset commit `c54ced59`, with bytes and SHA-256 (= the Hugging Face LFS oid). |
| `months.tsv` | **Denominator.** Per month: all live comments, and comments in each set. |
| `windows.parquet` | The unit: match sentence ±1 as `[start_char, end_char)` of the normalised comment, with set, term families, and BLAKE3 of the window and the comment. |

Rebuild and check from scratch:

    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py fetch    # 5.6 GB into .hncorpus/, SHA-256 checked
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py build    # byte-identical on rerun; verifies on completion
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py verify

Model output lives in `proposals/hacker-news/`, as witness proposals.

## Attribution and terms

This folder is **not** covered by the repository's CC0 dedication.

- **Source:** `open-index/hacker-news`
  (https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-index/hacker-news), licensed under the
  **Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY 1.0)**. Its items mirror the
  public Hacker News API (https://github.com/HackerNewsAPI/HN-API). The comments
  belong to their authors; this folder republishes none of their words.
- "Hacker News" is operated by Y Combinator; this corpus is not affiliated with
  or endorsed by it.

# S&P 500 earnings calls: AI corpus

Every passage in which a current S&P 500 company's earnings call mentions AI,
verbatim, byte-anchored, with the all-calls denominator. Method:
[`docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md`](../../docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md).

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: source parquet (HF dataset commit, bytes, BLAKE3, SHA-256 = HF LFS oid) and the Wikipedia revision defining the universe. |
| `sp500-constituents.tsv` | 503 tickers + CIKs from Wikipedia revision 1382178819. |
| `calls.tsv` | **Denominator.** Every S&P 500 call in the source, AI or not: paragraphs, duplicate share-class listing, AI paragraph and window counts. |
| `ai-paragraphs.parquet` | Every paragraph matching the AI term regex, verbatim, with BLAKE3. |
| `ai-windows.parquet` | The unit of analysis: match sentence ±1, as `[start_char, end_char)` of a stored paragraph, with BLAKE3. |
| `codebook-v0.1.tsv` | The NLI hypotheses the witnesses score. |
| `question-calls.tsv` | **Question denominator.** Per call: whether a Q&A was found, questioners, all questioner turns, AI questions. |
| `ai-questions.parquet` | Every AI question an outside questioner asked in the Q&A, the full turn verbatim, with BLAKE3 (`scripts/ec_questions.py`). |
| `codebook-questions-v0.1.tsv` | The NLI hypotheses for question intent: commercial, capital, threat, workforce, oversight. |

Rebuild and check from scratch:

    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py fetch          # 2.3 GB, verified against MANIFEST
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py constituents
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py build          # byte-identical outputs on rerun
    uv run scripts/ec_extract.py verify         # re-slice + re-hash every window
    uv run scripts/ec_questions.py build        # analyst questions; verifies against the source

Model output lives apart from the corpus, in `proposals/earnings-calls/`, because
it is a witness's proposal, not text.

## Attribution and terms

This folder is **not** covered by the repository's CC0 dedication.

- **Transcripts:** derived from the `defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data` dataset
  (https://huggingface.co/datasets/defeatbeta/yahoo-finance-data), table
  `stock_earning_call_transcripts`, commit `31ee0261`, licensed under the
  **Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-BY 1.0)**. That dataset states its
  transcripts are sourced from Yahoo Finance earnings-call pages and are intended
  for research and educational purposes. The words are the speakers'; this corpus
  republishes only the AI-mentioning paragraphs, for research.
- **S&P 500 constituent list:** derived from Wikipedia, "List of S&P 500
  companies", revision 1382178819, **CC BY-SA 4.0**.
- "S&P 500" is a trademark of S&P Dow Jones Indices LLC; this corpus is not
  affiliated with or endorsed by it.

# Hacker News: Anthropic and AI-security comments (IDs only)

Two focused sets of Hacker News comments, January 2021 to August 2026: those
that mention Anthropic or Claude, and those about AI security incidents (CVEs,
breaches, prompt injection, jailbreaks, leaked weights or keys). Method:
[`docs/hacker-news-corpus.md`](../../docs/hacker-news-corpus.md).

**No comment text and no usernames are stored here.** HN commenters are mostly
private individuals, so this folder holds item ids, character offsets into a
deterministic normalisation of each comment, and BLAKE3 hashes. The text is
rebuilt locally from the pinned source into the gitignored `.hncorpus/`, and
`verify` checks every hash. Any comment can be read at
`https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=<item_id>`.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: 68 monthly parquet files of `open-index/hacker-news` at dataset commit `c54ced59`, with bytes and SHA-256 (= the Hugging Face LFS oid). |
| `months.tsv` | **Denominator.** Per month: all live comments, and comments in each set. |
| `windows.parquet` | The unit: match sentence ±1 as `[start_char, end_char)` of the normalised comment, with set, term families, and BLAKE3 of the window and the comment. |

Rebuild and check from scratch:

    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py fetch    # 5.6 GB into .hncorpus/, SHA-256 checked
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py build    # byte-identical on rerun; verifies on completion
    uv run scripts/hn_extract.py verify

Model output lives in `proposals/hacker-news/`, as witness proposals.

verbatim, byte-anchored, with the all-calls denominator. Method:
[`docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md`](../../docs/earnings-call-ai-corpus.md).

# Democracy proxies: GDELT phrase timelines and Rooney Report toplines

Quick, citable proxy series for "health of democracy" as a public topic (how
often news and television say the words) and as stated attitudes (what
survey respondents tell the Notre Dame Health of Democracy Survey). Method and
limits: [`docs/democracy-proxies.md`](../../docs/democracy-proxies.md).

**None of these series measures any effect of Anthropic on democracy.** They
measure attention and stated attitudes. Anthropic co-mention counts show only
whether the company appears near the words.

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `MANIFEST.tsv` | Pins: every GDELT API response and every Rooney PDF/page, with request URL, bytes, SHA-256, BLAKE3 and as-of date. The bytes live in the gitignored `.democorpus/`. GDELT responses cannot be re-requested identically later, so the saved bytes are the pin. |
| `gdelt-timelines.tsv` | One row per (source, query, mode, series, period): `value` and `unit`. DOC rows from `timelinevolraw` also carry a `(norm)` series: total articles GDELT monitored that day. **As of 2026-11-04, 17 of 24 requests are pinned**: every TV response, and the DOC `timelinevol` responses except the `democracy` control. The DOC `democracy` control and all DOC `timelinevolraw` responses hit GDELT's rate limit (HTTP 429) and are marked `NOT PINNED` in `gdelt-summary.tsv`. |
| `gdelt-summary.tsv` | Per query: resolution, first and last period, periods with a non-zero value, peak period and value, and the sum. |
| `rooney-reports.tsv` | The 13 Rooney Reports linked from the listing page: PDF SHA-256, pages, embedded images per page (charts and logos, not extracted), and any AI-use disclosure, verbatim. |
| `rooney-transcription.tsv` | **Input, hand-transcribed.** Every percent stated in report text, with group, wave as stated, the report's wording, and a verbatim quote. |
| `rooney-toplines.tsv` | **Output.** The transcription after `build` has checked each quote against the page text of the pinned PDF and each percent against its quote, with the quote's BLAKE3. |
| `rooney-questionnaire.tsv` | **Input, hand-copied.** Item stems from the two questionnaires the Institute publishes as PDFs (October 2025, May 2026). |

content.content:
## 3. Hypotheses: the pattern as rates

Each hypothesis maps one paper move to one countable comparison. Thresholds,
effect floors, and α are **author decisions** (§8, D2) — none is stated in the
paper, whose falsifiers are document-level. Any number used must be
pre-registered in the versioned codebook (§6) before test data is seen, or
the headline rate is threshold-shoppable.

| # | Paper move | Rate that must differ | Fails if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | "Aspirational conditions, not metrics" (§2 table) | Commitment-strength + dated/metric slot completeness: Report pillar commitments vs section-matched S-1 binding covenants | Equal or reversed under section-matched permutation test |
| H2 | Input-for-outcome substitution (§3.2) | Share of extracted benefit commitments with a slot-verified filed *outcome* (not input) | Share ≥ pre-registered floor |
| H3 | Paradigm rhetoric, parameter acts (§1a) | Specificity density (numerals, dates, entities, citations per 100 tokens): benefit sentences vs risk/financial sentences | Benefit ≥ risk/financial |
| H4 | Attribution asymmetry (§3.5) | `actor = Anthropic` rate for benefits vs for harms (industry / perception / passive) | Rates equal |
| H5 | Future-benefit discounting (§3.1) | Undated-future vs dated-future commitments | Dated ≥ undated |

Scope limit, stated once and binding on every result slide thereafter:
H1–H5 measure **register divergence inside filed text**. They corroborate
the paper's textual pattern. They do not corroborate world outcomes, and no
wording in any output may upgrade them to that claim. Outcome corroboration
is §6.4 or it does not happen.

What already exists is **not gold** for any of these. The 60 fragments are a
quote audit, not span annotations. The 234 Descartes claim rows prove quote
occurrence only. Appendix C verdicts are the paper's conclusions; training
or validating on them grades the paper with its own answer key — the
self-grading move §3.4 names. Gold must be created (§6.1).

## 4. Pipeline, in build order
## 6. Validation

### 6.1 Gold

Stratified random sample (document × section), never model-selected. Two
independent annotators under the versioned codebook; per-label κ/α
published; third-human adjudication; unadjudicable items kept as recorded
conflicts, never force-labelled. Train/dev/test split **by section**, never
by random sentence — adjacent sentences share boilerplate and defined
terms, so sentence-level splits leak. The codebook, taxonomy, modality
lexicon, and every threshold live in versioned files ingested as artifacts,
so each result pins the exact definitions it ran under
([`epistemics.md`](epistemics.md) on frameworks).

### 6.2 Calibration and error analysis

Temperature or isotonic calibration on dev only. Report ECE, Brier score,
and full PR curves on held-out test — never a single F1 at a tuned
threshold. Every headline rate reported across a pre-registered threshold
range. Error analysis stratified by section type, sentence length, and
numeric density; every false "entail" on a load-bearing claim gets a named
error record. Below the pre-registered confidence band the system abstains
and records the abstention. (Note: an abstained derivation is not a pass —
the spec's skipped rule makes a plain run fail. Route A proposals may
abstain freely; Route B may not exist until it can stop abstaining
deterministically.)

### 6.3 Controls. Mandatory, not polish.

- **Shuffled placebo:** permuted promise↔act pairs must collapse to neutral
  at a pre-registered rate.
- **Peer control:** identical frozen pipeline on a non-PBC S-1.
- **Comparator control:** identical pipeline on another benefit report +
  filing pair.
- **Mandated hedging:** forward-looking safe-harbour language labelled
  `mandated` and excluded from evasion counts. A modality counter without
  this stratum rediscovers securities law and calls it deceit.
- **Section and length matching:** every cross-document rate computed
  within matched sections, length-stratified. Raw Report-vs-S-1 hedging
  rates are uninterpretable and must not be published.

### 6.4 Independence: the outcome join

Text rates need an external spine or they stay genre measurement. Two joins
provide it. First, the paper's own §8 falsifier documents, checked for a
sample of extracted promises. Second, the enforcement/incident join
designed in Appendix E of the working paper (data corpus: the Index run on
the S&P 500 — in the working tree at the time of writing, uncommitted):
disclosed risk (Item 1A) joined to governing mechanism (Item 106, Rule
10D-1 exhibits, DEF 14A) and to realized incidents (8-K Items 1.05/8.01,
litigation releases, AAERs). Appendix E's stated falsifier is the right
one and this spec adopts it verbatim in spirit: if low mechanism coverage
does not predict later enforcement, incidents, or restatements, the index
is decoration, and we will say so. Its cyber-first pilot — risk, mechanism,
and incident all inside SEC filings — is also the right first control
corpus for Stage 4, because it supplies realized outcomes at filing scale.
EDGAR full text and EDGAR-CORPUS give the negative-control universe the
single-company design lacks. Rater design follows Appendix E: every
model-assigned rating enters at circle 3 with a byte-exact quote, three
independent labellers, disagreement published (GOV-5 applied to ourselves).

## 10. Results log

*v0.1 (2026-11-03): empty. No corpus ingested, no annotation run, no model run.*

### 2026-11-04 · Earnings-call AI windows, codebook v0.1, two NLI witnesses

**Status: witness proposals only.** No human gold set exists for this
codebook, so precision and recall are unknown and go criterion (a) in §7 is
not met. No count below is citable as a rate of anything except witness
agreement. Method: [`earnings-call-ai-corpus.md`](earnings-call-ai-corpus.md).

- **Input.** 38,600 windows from 33,622 unique, non-stub S&P 500 calls
  (fiscal 2005–2027), scored against 16 hypotheses: 617,600 pairs per witness.
- **Witnesses.** DeBERTa-v3-large and ModernBERT-large zero-shot NLI at pinned
  revisions, bfloat16 on Modal L40S. Outputs:
  `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/deberta.parquet` (BLAKE3 `e3f0601b…`)
  and `modernbert.parquet` (`740db8fd…`). The full pins are in `run-*.json`.
- **Agreement** (`report/agreement.tsv`). Cohen's κ is 0.70 for `about_ai`,
  0.61 for `ai_risk`, 0.53 for `ai_opportunity`, and 0.41 for `governance`.
  Across the 12 risk types κ ranges from 0.26 (`disruption`) to 0.69
  (`energy`). The witnesses differ most on `capex` (231 vs 639 positives),
  `disruption` (357 vs 87) and `safety_ethics` (429 vs 875). Those are the
  first hypotheses to put in front of a human coder.
- **Proposed positives** (both witnesses ≥ 0.5). 6,427 calls have at least
  one window about AI, 251 have a proposed `ai_risk` window, and 68 have a
  proposed `governance` window. 125 of the 251 `ai_risk` calls fall in fiscal 2026.
  Analyst-heuristic windows are proposed as risk at 3.1% of their AI windows,
  against 1.2% for issuer-heuristic windows (`report/by-role.tsv`).
- **Next gate.** Draw a stratified hand-coded sample, oversampling the
  disagreement cells above, and report precision and recall per hypothesis
  before any rate leaves `proposals/`.



### 2026-11-04 · Analyst questions about AI, codebook-questions v0.1

**Status: witness proposals only.** There is no gold set yet; the sample is
in `gold/earnings-calls/`. Method:
[`earnings-call-ai-corpus.md`](earnings-call-ai-corpus.md) §10.

- **Input.** 4,288 AI questions asked by outside questioners on S&P 500 calls,
  scored against 10 intent hypotheses by the same two witnesses on Modal L40S.
- **Agreement** (`codebook-questions-v0.1/report/agreement.tsv`). κ runs from
  0.32 (`q_harm`, only 4 joint positives) to 0.74 (`q_security`), with
  `q_revenue` at 0.62 and `q_controls` at 0.48.
- **12 months to 2026-11-04.** There were 1,645 AI questions from 654
  questioners on 293 firms (`report/ttm.tsv`).
  - **Selling or spending on AI:** 21.2% revenue, demand or pricing; 8.7% AI
    spending and its return; 4.7% cost savings.
  - **Governing its risks:** 3.0% security or privacy; 2.9% risks or
    downsides; 0.8% (13 questions) how the company controls or governs AI
    risk; 0.3% regulation or liability; 0.2% harm to customers or society.
- **Word cross-check, calendar 2026.** 50.4% of AI questions use a commercial
  word and 2.2% use an oversight word. The direction matches the witnesses.
- **Read of the verbatim oversight questions.** Most frame risk as exposure of
  the firm's own earnings, such as an insurer's AI liability book or deposits
  drained by AI agents. Few ask about harm to anyone else. This is a reading,
  not a count, until the gold set is coded.

### 2026-11-04 · Hacker News: Anthropic and AI-security comments, codebook v0.1

**Status: witness proposals only; no gold set.** Method:
[`hacker-news-corpus.md`](hacker-news-corpus.md). The repository holds ids,
offsets and hashes, never comment text.

- **Input.** `open-index/hacker-news` @ `c54ced59`, 2021-01 to 2026-08:
  118,321 windows on 111,662 comments. The anthropic set has 105,559
  windows and the ai_security set 12,762. Both witnesses ran on Modal L40S
  against the unchanged `codebook-v0.1.tsv`.
- **Agreement** (`proposals/hacker-news/report/agreement.tsv`). κ on
  `ai_risk` is 0.54 in both sets, against 0.61 on calls.
  `safety_ethics` drops to 0.52 (anthropic) and 0.24 (ai_security), and
  `governance` to about 0.3.
- **Precision read.** On HN, `safety_ethics` and `regulation` take in
  general grievances: outages, terms of service, spending. A spot check
  of 6 windows each found roughly half off-topic for `regulation`. The HN
  type shares are therefore not comparable to calls in level, only in
  rough order.
- **Volume** (`report/by-month.tsv`). Anthropic comments rose from about
  1,000 a month in early 2025 to 8,500–9,800 a month from February to July
  2026. The share proposed as `ai_risk` rose from about 3.6% to 7–12%.

## 3. Hypotheses: the pattern as rates

Each hypothesis maps one paper move to one countable comparison. Thresholds,
effect floors, and α are **author decisions** (§8, D2) — none is stated in the
paper, whose falsifiers are document-level. Any number used must be
pre-registered in the versioned codebook (§6) before test data is seen, or
the headline rate is threshold-shoppable.

| # | Paper move | Rate that must differ | Fails if |
|---|---|---|---|
| H1 | "Aspirational conditions, not metrics" (§2 table) | Commitment-strength + dated/metric slot completeness: Report pillar commitments vs section-matched S-1 binding covenants | Equal or reversed under section-matched permutation test |
| H2 | Input-for-outcome substitution (§3.2) | Share of extracted benefit commitments with a slot-verified filed *outcome* (not input) | Share ≥ pre-registered floor |
| H3 | Paradigm rhetoric, parameter acts (§1a) | Specificity density (numerals, dates, entities, citations per 100 tokens): benefit sentences vs risk/financial sentences | Benefit ≥ risk/financial |
| H4 | Attribution asymmetry (§3.5) | `actor = Anthropic` rate for benefits vs for harms (industry / perception / passive) | Rates equal |
| H5 | Future-benefit discounting (§3.1) | Undated-future vs dated-future commitments | Dated ≥ undated |

Scope limit, stated once and binding on every result slide thereafter:
H1–H5 measure **register divergence inside filed text**. They corroborate
the paper's textual pattern. They do not corroborate world outcomes, and no
wording in any output may upgrade them to that claim. Outcome corroboration
is §6.4 or it does not happen.

What already exists is **not gold** for any of these. The 60 fragments are a
quote audit, not span annotations. The 234 Descartes claim rows prove quote
occurrence only. Appendix C verdicts are the paper's conclusions; training
or validating on them grades the paper with its own answer key — the
self-grading move §3.4 names. Gold must be created (§6.1).

## 4. Pipeline, in build order
## 6. Validation

### 6.1 Gold

Stratified random sample (document × section), never model-selected. Two
independent annotators under the versioned codebook; per-label κ/α
published; third-human adjudication; unadjudicable items kept as recorded
conflicts, never force-labelled. Train/dev/test split **by section**, never
by random sentence — adjacent sentences share boilerplate and defined
terms, so sentence-level splits leak. The codebook, taxonomy, modality
lexicon, and every threshold live in versioned files ingested as artifacts,
so each result pins the exact definitions it ran under
([`epistemics.md`](epistemics.md) on frameworks).

### 6.2 Calibration and error analysis

Temperature or isotonic calibration on dev only. Report ECE, Brier score,
and full PR curves on held-out test — never a single F1 at a tuned
threshold. Every headline rate reported across a pre-registered threshold
range. Error analysis stratified by section type, sentence length, and
numeric density; every false "entail" on a load-bearing claim gets a named
error record. Below the pre-registered confidence band the system abstains
and records the abstention. (Note: an abstained derivation is not a pass —
the spec's skipped rule makes a plain run fail. Route A proposals may
abstain freely; Route B may not exist until it can stop abstaining
deterministically.)

### 6.3 Controls. Mandatory, not polish.

- **Shuffled placebo:** permuted promise↔act pairs must collapse to neutral
  at a pre-registered rate.
- **Peer control:** identical frozen pipeline on a non-PBC S-1.
- **Comparator control:** identical pipeline on another benefit report +
  filing pair.
- **Mandated hedging:** forward-looking safe-harbour language labelled
  `mandated` and excluded from evasion counts. A modality counter without
  this stratum rediscovers securities law and calls it deceit.
- **Section and length matching:** every cross-document rate computed
  within matched sections, length-stratified. Raw Report-vs-S-1 hedging
  rates are uninterpretable and must not be published.

### 6.4 Independence: the outcome join

Text rates need an external spine or they stay genre measurement. Two joins
provide it. First, the paper's own §8 falsifier documents, checked for a
sample of extracted promises. Second, the enforcement/incident join
designed in Appendix E of the working paper (data corpus: the Index run on
the S&P 500 — in the working tree at the time of writing, uncommitted):
disclosed risk (Item 1A) joined to governing mechanism (Item 106, Rule
10D-1 exhibits, DEF 14A) and to realized incidents (8-K Items 1.05/8.01,
litigation releases, AAERs). Appendix E's stated falsifier is the right
one and this spec adopts it verbatim in spirit: if low mechanism coverage
does not predict later enforcement, incidents, or restatements, the index
is decoration, and we will say so. Its cyber-first pilot — risk, mechanism,
and incident all inside SEC filings — is also the right first control
corpus for Stage 4, because it supplies realized outcomes at filing scale.
EDGAR full text and EDGAR-CORPUS give the negative-control universe the
single-company design lacks. Rater design follows Appendix E: every
model-assigned rating enters at circle 3 with a byte-exact quote, three
independent labellers, disagreement published (GOV-5 applied to ourselves).

input.message:
No accidental exposure. All scans printed file:line and pattern names only. The three email hits were checked by domain only. No credential files or environment dumps were read. The only network call fetched the defeatbeta Hugging Face card metadata to confirm its licence.

## Findings, ranked

**HIGH**

1. **Verbatim Yahoo-sourced transcripts are redistributed on a licence that probably cannot cover them.** The committed files are:
   - `corpus/earnings-calls/ai-paragraphs.parquet`: 28,602 verbatim paragraphs with speaker names.
   - `ai-windows.parquet`: 38,600 rows with text.
   - `ai-questions.parquet`: 4,288 full analyst turns.

   The only licence is the uploader's `odc-by` tag on HF. The defeatbeta card says the data is "sourced from Yahoo! Finance … via publicly available APIs … intended for research and educational purposes". ODC-BY covers database rights. It cannot grant copyright in transcripts that Yahoo or its transcript vendor owns, and Yahoo's terms bar redistribution. `corpus/earnings-calls/README.md` ("Attribution and terms") relies on the HF tag alone. This is the largest legal exposure in the repo. Storing ids and hashes plus rebuild-from-pin, as the HN corpus does, would remove it.

2. **The same transcript text sits outside the licence carve-out, so it is implicitly CC0.**
   - `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/risk-quotes-ttm.tsv` has a `quote` column with speaker names.
   - `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-questions-v0.1/report/oversight-questions.tsv` has a `question` column.
   - `gold/earnings-calls/*/sample.tsv` has a `text` column.

   AGENTS.md:10 says "Repo content is CC0 except `corpus/*/`", and README (License section, line 148) carves out only `corpus/earnings-calls/`. That publishes third-party words under a public-domain dedication.

3. **DECK.md publishes rates that the repo's own spec says may not leave `proposals/`.** `docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md` §10 (around lines 413–416 and 437–439) says "No count below is citable as a rate of anything except witness agreement" and sets a gate: precision and recall per hypothesis "before any rate leaves `proposals/`". `gold/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/score.tsv:1` says "0 of 240 sample rows coded". The deck still captions rates as facts ("12.2% of 2026 S&P 500 calls", "137 firms"). A small grey disclaimer tag does not cure captions written as findings.

4. **The dialogue-space slide makes a cross-source level comparison that the spec explicitly disowns.** The spec's HN entry says HN type shares "are therefore not comparable to calls in level, only in rough order". It also says a spot check found about half of HN `regulation` windows off-topic. The deck slide nonetheless compares levels: 10% executives vs 39% HN vs 61% Wikipedia.
   - The 61% for Wikipedia is partly built in. The 14 new v0.2 dimensions were read from Wikipedia's AI-risk headings and then scored on those same AI-risk articles.
   - The executive base is 179 units, so its cells rest on a handful of passages.

**MEDIUM**

5. **Forking paths.** The public deck uses `v0.2-draft`, whose wording is unreviewed (OPENQUESTIONS Q2), rather than v0.1. The two give different headline numbers: committed v0.1 `risk-ranking-ttm.tsv` has Cyber 39 and capex 27, while the deck has 40 and 26.
   - The threshold of 0.5 with both witnesses agreeing is not pre-registered and has no sensitivity range. Spec §3 and §6.2 require both and call an unregistered threshold "threshold-shoppable".
   - Witness agreement is weak on several risk types: κ 0.26–0.41 for disruption, capex, bias, privacy, safety_ethics and governance (`report/agreement.tsv`).
   - bf16 scores move with batch composition (spec §10, v0.2 entry).

6. **The intent slide picks an extreme pair.** "21.2% sells vs 0.8% controls" sets the broadest commercial category against the narrowest governance category: 13 questions, κ 0.48. The spec lists the other governance intents: security or privacy 3.0% and risks 2.9%. A summed comparison is still lopsided but honest.

7. **Licence metadata is inconsistent.** `.zenodo.json:9` (`"license": "cc-zero"`) and `CITATION.cff:19` (`CC0-1.0`) label the whole deposit CC0. The corpora are actually ODC-BY, CC BY-SA 4.0, CC BY, CVE terms and Notre Dame copyright. A Zenodo upload would mislicense them.

8. **Survivorship and partial year.** The earnings universe is today's S&P 500 (pinned Wikipedia revision). 2026 runs to 11-04, and calendar-year binning mixes fiscal quarters. The caveats are stated on the last slide only, not beside the trend chart.

9. **Attribution conflict for a registered investment adviser.** README ("Author") says "Personal research; not published … by Ethical Capital". But `corpus/codebooks/codebook-v0.2-draft.meta.yml` has "producer: Ethical Capital" and "citation_full: Ethical Capital …". SEC user-agent strings carry firm emails (`scripts/rf_extract.py:51`, `scripts/rf_loss.py:49`, `scripts/democracy_proxies.py:62`; business addresses, not secrets). A firm-attributed critique of a named company may trigger marketing-rule review.

**LOW**

10. **HN corpus complies.** `windows.parquet` holds ids, offsets and BLAKE3 hashes; the proposals parquets hold `window_id`/`hypothesis_id`/`p_entail`; `examples-ttm.tsv` holds item ids and URLs. No comment text or usernames are stored. Residual risk: item ids resolve to authors, and the reports label individual comments with risk types.
11. **CVE, Epoch, Wikipedia and Rooney are fine.**
   - CVE stores no record text.
   - The 67 Epoch `*_external.csv` third-party tables are correctly left out (0 tracked), and YouGov data is excluded.
   - Wikipedia carries the CC BY-SA ShareAlike notice.
   - Rooney uses short quotes only.
12. **Secrets and infrastructure.** No AWS, GitHub, HF, `sk-`, Slack, JWT, PEM, credentialled DSN or key-assignment patterns were found. No private hostnames, tailnet IPs or home paths were found. `docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md:559` names the build host's timezone (America/Denver), which is harmless. `.claude/settings.json` and `.entire/settings.json` are tracked; they hold only hook commands, but this contradicts the AGENTS.md "never stage `.claude/`" rule.
13. **Fairness of the paper.** The deck's §365(b)/§367 summary is accurate. The paper covers the Long-Term Benefit Trust (14 mentions) and gives explicit per-section falsifiers (`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md:713, 743, 774, 811, 848`). The CVE slide fairly says it "cannot confirm or refute" 33,000+. "Legally toothless" is opinion, and its basis is disclosed. I found nothing defamatory. The deck's argument slide omits the trust, which a hostile reader will call selective.

## Weakest inferential link

The lead chart (DECK.md:58) says "AI framed as a risk: 12.2% of 2026 calls … against at most 0.6% in any year before 2023". That is a call-level "any window positive" metric built on unvalidated labels where both models must agree. Calls with an AI mention grew from about 1 AI window per call in 2022 to about 5.7 in 2026. So with any constant false-positive rate, the call-level rate rises with the volume of AI talk alone.

The per-AI-window risk rate is nearly flat from 2022 to 2024 (`proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/by-year.tsv`, fiscal years, v0.1):

| Fiscal year | Risk windows | AI windows | Rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2022 | 3 | 385 | 0.8% |
| 2023 | 22 | 2,175 | 1.0% |
| 2024 | 33 | 3,317 | 1.0% |
| 2025 | 66 | 4,324 | 1.5% |
| 2026 | 191 | 5,875 | 3.3% |

So most of the pre/post-2023 contrast is AI-mention volume multiplied by an unmeasured error rate, not a shift in framing. Any real framing change shows up only in 2025–26, and even that is unverified until the 240-row gold sample is coded.

## Verdict

The repo is unusually honest in its internals. It states denominators, logs agreement, admits the bf16 non-reproducibility and the bio_chem wording failure, keeps HN text out, and leaves Epoch's external tables out. But the public deck outruns the method: it states witness proposals as rates, compares levels across sources that the spec says are not comparable, and leads with a call-level trend confounded by mention volume. All of this sits on a draft codebook with no gold labels. Legally, the serious problem is redistributing verbatim Yahoo-sourced transcripts, worse where they sit under the CC0 dedication in `proposals/` and `gold/`. The defeatbeta ODC-BY tag probably cannot authorise that, and the Zenodo/CFF CC0 metadata compounds it. Before publication, I would:
1. Convert the earnings corpus and its quote tables to ids, offsets and hashes.
2. Fix the licence metadata.
3. Hold every deck rate until the gold set is coded, or recaption the rates as witness agreement.
4. Report the risk trend per AI window.
